transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Jared Cole (Eloquent - Head of ML), Nina Patel (Eloquent - Platform Lead), Marco Ruiz (Eloquent - CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining for the Q1 QBR, appreciate you making time. Priya and Liam are with me from Redwood. How are you all doing?
[00:08] Jared: Good, thanks. Busy month, saw a big uptick in queries.
[00:12] Nina: Yeah traffic spiked — some batch jobs hitting our reranker route.
[00:18] Priya: We can walk through the usage charts and then dig into the reliability notes.
[00:25] Liam: Quick intro from me, I ran the February runbook, looked at p95 tails, and we flagged two short incidents on 02/14 and 02/24.

[00:35] Maya: To kick off, high level numbers: your token consumption was up ~32% month-over-month, reranker routes are the cost hot spots, and there were two brief error spikes that coincided with a model fallback event. We also noticed an increase in latency for long context prompts.
[00:50] Jared: Right, the increase came after we rolled the new retrieval pipeline. The reranker is called a lot more now, it's ballooning our cost.
[00:58] Nina: We got surprised by the cost in the last invoice; can you show us the per-route breakdown?
[01:05] Maya: Absolutely, we'll send a detailed export after the call but high level — reranker + long-context generation routes are ~65% of the bill despite being 20% of requests. That's due to model choices and sequence lengths.
[01:20] Marco: On the SLA and procurement side, procurement needs SOC 2 and KMS diagrams. We're also evaluating moving sensitive workloads into a Dedicated or Private deployment.
[01:30] Priya: We can provide SOC 2 artifacts and a KMS integration guide. Note that Private deployments require a separate procurement track, but Dedicated is commonly used for predictability.

[01:45] Liam: Technical note — the February incidents were due to a model fallback that retried to a larger variant when a particular node was overloaded, which caused transient queueing and a small error burst. We have two mitigations: capacity reservations and smarter fallback limits.
[02:05] Jared: Can you explain the fallback behavior? We saw requests get routed to a different region and latency spiked.
[02:12] Liam: The smart routing policy will prefer lower-latency zones but when local capacity is constrained it routes to compatible variants; in your case the variant had a cold KV cache which added ~400ms. We can tune routing policies to prefer same-region fallbacks or enforce stricter variant compatibility.
[02:28] Maya: There's also the Dedicated option where you reserve GPU pools and avoid noisy neighbor effects; that would reduce fallbacks.
[02:35] Nina: What's the delta in cost vs hosted? We're sensitive to both SLOs and unit cost.
[02:42] Maya: Typical Dedicated reserved pricing gives you 20–40% better unit cost at commit, but there are ops and sizing considerations. We should run a quick sizing exercise — Liam can run benchmarks against a Dedicated config.
[02:55] Marco: We need an ROI calc. If we commit to Dedicated, what commit level does our current usage map to?
[03:03] Maya: We'll map your top routes and token patterns to an estimated GPU footprint and show break-even points. We'll send that in the cost breakdown.

[03:15] Priya: On reliability, action items for us: provide the incident timeline, remediation steps we applied, and recommended routing policy changes.
[03:25] Jared: The incident timeline will help our postmortem. Also, can we get logs from the two incidents?
[03:30] Liam: Yes, I'll export the request traces and the fallback logs. Some of the labels in the traces may be slightly off due to transcription and sampling — the trace ids are still valid.

[03:40] Nina: Security question — if we move to Dedicated or Private, how does KMS integration work with our existing HSM? We need to know key wrapping and encryption-at-rest details.
[03:50] Priya: We support customer-managed keys via supported KMS/HSM solutions; we'll provide KMS architecture diagrams and a short integration checklist. For Private deployments we can support on-prem HSMs but that adds lead time.
[04:05] Marco: Any compliance gaps you see for our procurement team?
[04:08] Priya: Not major; we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts. For auditor requests we can provide audit logs and data residency notes. We'll share the artifact pack.

[04:20] Maya: On roadmap alignment — you're interested in lower-cost reranking, improved batching on the routing tier, and quantization profiles. Research is actively exploring new quantization-friendly kernels. We can prioritise a focused evaluation for your reranker workload.
[04:34] Jared: That would be helpful; a quantization profile that preserves rerank quality but reduces GPU time is ideal.
[04:40] Liam: We can run a small eval: run your top 200 prompts vs quantized variants and measure latency and nDCG drop. We recommend starting with int8 and monitoring regression alerts.
[04:52] Nina: Ok, timeline?
[04:55] Liam: I can run a quick 1-hour bench and share results within a week if you provide example prompts and a snapshot of reranker weights.
[05:03] Marco: Procurement will also want a short pilot contract and a 90-day SLA addendum for Dedicated.
[05:09] Maya: We'll loop in Sales Ops to draft terms once you signal intent.

[05:15] Priya: Recap: we'll send the cost breakdown, SOC 2/KMS docs, incident logs, and a proposed Dedicated sizing plan.
[05:23] Jared: Sounds good. Can you put the cost per route in CSV form? That helps our finance team.
[05:28] Maya: Yes, CSV and a one-pager ROI summary.
[05:32] Nina: Also tag any suggested quick wins — e.g., batch window changes or cache TTL tuning.
[05:37] Liam: Will do. There are a couple low-effort wins: reduce reranker sequence length for non-critical pages and enable prefix caching for recurrent requests.
[05:47] Marco: Great, thanks everyone.
[05:50] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up on the action items.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard product names (we heard "Redwood Dedicate" once), filler words, and timestamp sampling every 30–60s. The transcript preserves speech disfluency and overlapping talk in a few spots.
